newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan aluminium buyers stock up, fear price hike.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan aluminium buyers stock up, fear price hike.

text.p: Taiwan buyers have begun stockpiling aluminium ingots in anticipation of further price rises following a sharp international price increase in January alone, metal traders said on Tuesday.
"Many aluminium buyers are increasing their inventory levels as they expect a continued price rise," a China Steel Aluminium Co buyer told Reuters by telephone.
Local aluminium ingot prices have already soared more than 30 percent since January and could rise further, traders said.
Traders attributed the rise to a jump in scrap material prices to over 58 U.S. cents per pound from 47 U.S. cents in barely a month.
Taiwan imported some 480,000 tonnes of gross aluminium in 1995, up from 1994's 450,000 tonne. Figures for 1996 are not yet available.
